# Tally Forms — Style Reference

> Ballpoint doodles in the margins of a white notebook, one magenta highlighter. Inter in warm Notion ink sits on a #ffffff page, translucent hairlines frame each block, a blue pen signs every action, and magenta is kept for underlining.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Tally runs a notebook-margin product language. The page behaves like a document, and the decoration is drawn in ballpoint. The canvas is #ffffff, cards sit on a near-identical #fefefe, and secondary fills step down to #eaeaea and #dfdfde, so surfaces separate through hairlines and soft shadow rather than tone. The chromatic budget is two hues, each with one job: #0070d7 blue fills every action (hero CTA, nav CTA, Publish), and #f81ce5 magenta appears only in doodles, squiggle underlines, feature icons and one ringed callout. Typography is Inter throughout. Headlines are weight 700 in pure #000000 at 64px with -2px tracking, card titles are 800 at 18px, and body text is Notion's warm #37352f at 16px/1.5 (120 uses). Hierarchy therefore comes from weight and from the jump from warm ink to true black, not from a tidy modular ratio. Shapes are soft: 8px buttons, 10px cards, 7px nav items. Elevation is a warm-tinted, multi-layer shadow ring. The page reads as a friendly writing tool rather than a SaaS dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page background, nav background and button label text (7 text uses). It is deliberately pure white, so the ballpoint doodles read as ink on paper rather than as decoration on a tinted panel. |
| Paper Card | `#fefefe` | `--color-paper-card` | Feature cards, the product mockup window and the floating help button (13 uses). It sits one step off white, so cards separate by hairline and shadow, not by fill. |
| Fog Surface | `#eaeaea` | `--color-fog-surface` | Secondary fills inside the mockup and hover tints on quiet controls (3 uses). It is the only true tonal step, rationed to keep the page flat. |
| Pebble Dot | `#dfdfde` | `--color-pebble-dot` | Mockup traffic-light dots, rule strokes and placeholder fills (21 uses). It is a warm neutral that belongs to the ink family. Do not use it as a card background. |
| Jet Headline | `#000000` | `--color-jet-headline` | H1, H2 and H3 text (33 text uses) and the black secondary button fill. Pure black is reserved for display weight, which makes headings land harder than the warm body ink. |
| Ink | `#37352f` | `--color-ink` | Body paragraphs, ledes, nav links and footer text (120+ uses, the workhorse). This warm near-black is borrowed from document editors and makes the page read as a doc. |
| Graphite Body | `#45433e` | `--color-graphite-body` | Mockup copy, logo-strip caption and secondary paragraphs (38 uses). It is one shade lighter than Ink and supports dense supporting text without a visible gray jump. |
| Pewter Caption | `#5f5e5a` | `--color-pewter-caption` | Testimonial quote, attribution titles and microcopy such as "No signup required" (38 uses). It is the caption voice that recedes politely. |
| Ash Hint | `#777672` | `--color-ash-hint` | Placeholder text, input hints and the faintest UI labels (9 uses). It marks the floor of the text ladder. Do not set body copy in it. |
| Ink Hairline | `#37352f17` | `--color-ink-hairline` | 2px card borders (7 uses), the 1px footer top rule and mockup dividers. Translucent Ink at roughly 9% keeps every line in the same warm temperature as the text. |
| Cobalt Signal | `#0070d7` | `--color-cobalt-signal` | Hero CTA, nav "Create form" pill, mockup Publish button and link color. It is the only color that means "act". Do not use it for decoration or headings. |
| Fuchsia Marker | `#f81ce5` | `--color-fuchsia-marker` | Squiggle underlines, doodle confetti, feature icons and the highlight card ring. It is the highlighter, decorative punctuation only. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Inter — the single family for display, UI and body, separated by weight rather than by face · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter is open-source, so self-host it at the measured weights first. If a swap is required, Geist at the same weights renders a touch narrower but matches stroke thickness. Public Sans draws slightly lighter than nominal, so use 500 for body and 800 for 700 headlines to match visual weight. Inter itself renders true to its nominal weights.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700, 800
- **Sizes:** 13px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 22px, 26px, 30px, 36px, 64px
- **Line height:** 1.0 (64px display, 14px and 15px labels), 1.15 (13px to 36px headings), 1.25 (22px lede), 1.5 (16px body), 1.8 (15px card copy)
- **Letter spacing:** -2px at 64px (-0.031em); 0 at every other size
- **Role:** One family carries everything, so the system speaks through weight. It uses five weights where most marketing sites use three, and the inversion is the signature: 18px card titles at 800 are heavier than 36px section headings at 700, so small labels hit with the punch usually reserved for display. The scale is irregular rather than modular. 36 to 64 is a 1.78 jump, far past a Perfect Fourth (1.333), which makes the hero headline dramatically oversized against everything below it. Tracking is used once, at -2px on the 64px headline, to tighten it into a single shape.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 400 | 13px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 600 | 14px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 15px | 1.8 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 500 | 22px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 800 | 18px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Inter | 800 | 26px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Inter | 700 | 30px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Inter | 700 | 36px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Inter | 700 | 64px | 1.0 | -2px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set body copy in #37352f at 16px/1.5 weight 400 — the warm ink is what makes the page read as a doc rather than a landing page.
- Reserve #000000 for headings at 18px and above — the step from warm ink to true black carries hierarchy as much as size does.
- Fill every primary action with #0070d7 at 8px radius and 36px height — blue is the only color that means "click", and the small height keeps it tool-like.
- Use #f81ce5 only as a stroke: squiggles, confetti dashes, 16px icons and the 2px ring — magenta is the highlighter pen, punctuation rather than decoration.
- Draw illustrations as monochrome #37352f ballpoint linework with sparse magenta accents — the hand-drawn layer is the signature and must stay sketchbook-thin.
- Separate cards with a 2px #37352f17 border plus shadow md on #fefefe — elevation should feel like a sheet lifted 3px off the page, not a floating panel.
- Leave 192px between major sections and cap text columns at 600px — the generous vertical rhythm is what keeps a five-weight type system from feeling busy.

### Don't

- Don't make the CTA larger to add urgency, for example a 56px-tall button with 24px padding — the 36px control at 15px/600 is part of the editor metaphor, and inflating it turns the doc into an ad.
- Don't render doodles in full color or as polished vector mascots — the thesis is ballpoint marginalia, and #37352f linework with magenta accents is non-negotiable.
- Don't use #f81ce5 as a button fill, link color or section background — once magenta means "act", the blue #0070d7 loses its monopoly and the two-hue budget collapses.
- Don't swap #37352f for a cool neutral gray like a slate blue-gray — cool grays fight the warm-tinted 61,59,53 shadow layers and the translucent warm hairlines.
- Don't add a gradient hero backdrop or glowing orbs behind the 64px headline — the canvas is #ffffff paper, and atmosphere comes from sketches, not light effects.
- Don't set section headings heavier than card titles, for example a 36px heading at 800 — the 700 heading over 800 subheading inversion keeps big type calm and small type punchy.
- Never outline the secondary button in a 1px border on white — the secondary action is solid #000000 at identical geometry, so hierarchy reads through hue, not fill.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #fefefe (Paper Card)
- body text: #37352f (Ink)
- headings: #000000 (Jet Headline)
- caption text: #5f5e5a (Pewter Caption)
- hairline: #37352f17 (Ink Hairline)
- decorative accent: #f81ce5 (Fuchsia Marker)
- primary action: #0070d7 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and progress bars stay neutral, using #37352f for primary series, #dfdfde for tracks and #0070d7 only for the one series the user can act on, with #f81ce5 limited to a single 2px highlight stroke and never used as a solid fill.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: a `<button>` with background #0070d7, label color #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 0 14px, height 36px, font Inter 15px weight 600 with line-height 1.0, and a 14px right-arrow icon after the label with an 8px gap. No shadow. Pair it with a secondary button of identical geometry and type but background #000000, with an 8px gap between the two. Below the primary, add microcopy reading "No signup required" in Inter 13px weight 400 color #5f5e5a, 8px beneath.

2. Build a hero section on a #ffffff canvas with a 976px max-width, centered text and 128px top padding. Headline "The simplest way to create forms" in Inter 64px weight 700, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -2px, color #000000. Under one word, place a hand-drawn SVG squiggle stroke in #f81ce5, 2px wide. Then a 600px-max lede in Inter 22px weight 500, line-height 1.25, color #37352f, 16px below. Then the 36px #0070d7 CTA, 32px below. Then a mockup window 64px below: surface #fefefe, border 2px solid #37352f17, border-radius 10px, box-shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.09) 0 3px 12px 0, with three 8px #dfdfde circular dots top-left. Scatter monochrome #37352f line doodles in both gutters.

3. Build a feature card: background #fefefe, border 2px solid #37352f17, border-radius 10px, padding 20px, box-shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.09) 0 3px 12px 0. Inside, from top to bottom: a 16px line icon in #f81ce5, a 16px gap, a title in Inter 18px weight 800, line-height 1.15, color #000000, an 8px gap, then body copy in Inter 15px weight 400, line-height 1.8, color #37352f. Place two cards side by side with a 20px gap. For the single highlight variant, replace the border and shadow with box-shadow rgb(248,28,229) 0 0 0 2px, rgba(248,28,229,0.36) 0 0 0 4px and set the title at 26px weight 800.

4. Build a navigation bar: height 60px, background #ffffff, static (not sticky), horizontal padding 16px, with no bottom border. Put a black hand-lettered wordmark on the left. On the right, add three text links (Pricing, Log in, Sign up) in Inter 14px weight 500, color #37352f, padding 0 10px, height 28px, border-radius 7px, with an #eaeaea background on hover, spaced 8px apart. Finish with a "Create form" pill: background #0070d7, color #ffffff, Inter 14px weight 600, padding 0 10px, height 28px, border-radius 7px.

**Density:** spacious

### Spacing Scale

| Name | Value | Token |

| sm | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 1px 0px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.16) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.08) 0px 3px 9px 0px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.08) 0px 2px 5px 0px` | `--shadow-sm` |

- **Page max-width:** 976px (600–976px)
- **Section gap:** 192px (64–192px)
- **Card padding:** 20px (20–32px)
- **Element gap:** 8px (4–32px)

## Components

### Primary Button — Cobalt Fill

**Role:** The single action color on the page

A compact blue pill-rectangle. Background #0070d7, label #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 0 14px, height 36px, Inter at 15px weight 600 with 1.0 line height, a trailing arrow glyph and no shadow. At 36px it is deliberately small against convention, where 44 to 56px hero CTAs are standard. The button behaves like an editor toolbar control rather than a billboard, which matches the "just start typing" promise.

### Secondary Button — Jet Fill

**Role:** Neutral action beside the blue CTA

An inverted twin. Background #000000, label #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 0 14px, height 36px, Inter 15px at 600, no shadow. It is used for "Browse templates" and the mockup's Submit button. Secondary actions are black rather than outlined, which is anti-convention: the hierarchy comes from hue (blue versus black) instead of fill versus ghost, so both buttons keep identical geometry and mass.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Static top strip, logo left

A borderless white strip. Background #ffffff, height 60px, not sticky (static positioning), with the hand-lettered "tally*" wordmark on the left and four items on the right separated by an 8px gap. Text links are Inter 14px weight 500 in #37352f with border-radius 7px, padding 0 10px and height 28px, gaining a #eaeaea tint on hover. The bar scrolls away with the page, which reads as a document header rather than an app chrome bar.

### Nav CTA Pill — Create Form

**Role:** Persistent small blue entry point

A miniature primary. Background #0070d7, label #ffffff, border-radius 7px, padding 0 10px, height 28px, Inter 14px at 600, no shadow. The 7px radius is a one-pixel step down from the 8px button radius, scaled proportionally for the 28px height. It is the only colored element in the nav, so the eye finds it immediately.

### Product Mockup Window

**Role:** Hero proof: the editor itself

A browser-frame screenshot rebuilt in HTML. Surface #fefefe, border 2px #37352f17, border-radius 10px, shadow md, three #dfdfde 50%-radius traffic-light dots, and a toolbar with a #0070d7 Publish button. The form inside uses Inter 30px weight 700 in #37352f, 4px-radius inputs and rating chips. The editor itself is the hero image, which proves the product rather than illustrating it.

### Feature Card

**Role:** Two-up and full-width benefit tiles

A hairline-bordered document block. Background #fefefe, border 2px solid #37352f17, border-radius 10px, padding 20px, shadow md. It holds a 16px #f81ce5 line icon, a title in Inter 18px weight 800 #000000 and body copy in Inter 15px/1.8 weight 400 #37352f. Lower halves carry embedded mini-demos such as pastel field tags or scrolling hash text. The 2px translucent border is heavier than the 1px convention but still faint at 9% opacity, a soft frame that never competes with the content.

### Highlight Card — Fuchsia Ring (Outlier)

**Role:** The one emphasized benefit

The system outlier. It shares the Feature Card's #fefefe surface, 10px radius and 20px padding, but swaps the hairline for shadow lg: a solid 2px #f81ce5 ring plus a 4px 36%-opacity halo. Its title, "Unlimited forms and submissions for free", is set at Inter 26px weight 800 in a violet-to-magenta gradient (decorative, not a system token), above a hand-drawn landscape. Magenta is allowed onto a container exactly once because the "free forever" claim is the brand's sharpest differentiator.

### Rating Scale Chip

**Role:** Mockup 0–10 linear scale cells

A tactile key cap. Background #ffffff, text #37352f in Inter 14px weight 500, border-radius 4px, padding 0 8px, height 28px, shadow sm (warm 1px ring plus two soft drops), arranged in a row with a 4px gap. The four-layer shadow makes each cell feel pressable without any color, and it is the system's template for interactive form controls.

### Logo Strip

**Role:** Social proof row of customers

A single horizontal row. A caption reading "Powering 2,500,000+ teams" in Inter 13px weight 400 #45433e sits above seven monochrome wordmarks (Notion, make, ghost, Brevo, Basedash, Pret, granola), rendered black at 18 to 26px height and spaced with a 32px gap on a #ffffff canvas, with no cards and no dividers. Monochrome is non-optional here because full-color logos would break the two-hue budget.

### Testimonial Quote

**Role:** Single centered endorsement

A pull quote without a container. Quote text is Inter 30px weight 700 in #5f5e5a with curly quote marks, centered, followed by a 32px gap and an attribution row: a 50%-radius hand-drawn avatar, the name in Inter 16px weight 600 #37352f and the title in Inter 13px weight 400 #5f5e5a. Setting a 30px bold quote in caption gray rather than black is the deliberate move, so it reads as overheard speech rather than a headline.

### Squiggle Underline

**Role:** Hand-drawn emphasis on one headline word

Ballpoint emphasis. A freehand SVG stroke in #f81ce5, roughly 2px wide, sits beneath a single word of a #000000 headline ("simplest", "but") with no background and no animation, and other decorative strokes in the same hue scatter as short dashes across the margins. It replaces bold, italic or gradient text as the emphasis device, which is how the brand signals personality without adding a third hue.

### Floating Help Button

**Role:** Persistent support entry, bottom-right

A small circular utility. Background #fefefe, glyph "?" in Inter 13px weight 600 #37352f, border-radius 50%, 24px diameter (estimated), shadow sm, fixed 20px from the bottom-right corner. It is the only fixed element on a page whose nav scrolls away, and it reads as an editor affordance rather than a chat bubble.

### Footer

**Role:** Wide link index, EU provenance

A quiet closing sheet. No background change, a 1px solid #37352f17 top border, padding 100px 0, width 976px, with link columns in Inter 16px weight 400 #37352f and a sign-off reading "Made and hosted in the EU" with a flag emoji. There is no dark footer slab, against the SaaS convention, so the document simply ends on paper.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set body copy in #37352f at 16px/1.5 weight 400 — the warm ink is what makes the page read as a doc rather than a landing page.
- Reserve #000000 for headings at 18px and above — the step from warm ink to true black carries hierarchy as much as size does.
- Fill every primary action with #0070d7 at 8px radius and 36px height — blue is the only color that means "click", and the small height keeps it tool-like.
- Use #f81ce5 only as a stroke: squiggles, confetti dashes, 16px icons and the 2px ring — magenta is the highlighter pen, punctuation rather than decoration.
- Draw illustrations as monochrome #37352f ballpoint linework with sparse magenta accents — the hand-drawn layer is the signature and must stay sketchbook-thin.
- Separate cards with a 2px #37352f17 border plus shadow md on #fefefe — elevation should feel like a sheet lifted 3px off the page, not a floating panel.
- Leave 192px between major sections and cap text columns at 600px — the generous vertical rhythm is what keeps a five-weight type system from feeling busy.

### Don't

- Don't make the CTA larger to add urgency, for example a 56px-tall button with 24px padding — the 36px control at 15px/600 is part of the editor metaphor, and inflating it turns the doc into an ad.
- Don't render doodles in full color or as polished vector mascots — the thesis is ballpoint marginalia, and #37352f linework with magenta accents is non-negotiable.
- Don't use #f81ce5 as a button fill, link color or section background — once magenta means "act", the blue #0070d7 loses its monopoly and the two-hue budget collapses.
- Don't swap #37352f for a cool neutral gray like a slate blue-gray — cool grays fight the warm-tinted 61,59,53 shadow layers and the translucent warm hairlines.
- Don't add a gradient hero backdrop or glowing orbs behind the 64px headline — the canvas is #ffffff paper, and atmosphere comes from sketches, not light effects.
- Don't set section headings heavier than card titles, for example a 36px heading at 800 — the 700 heading over 800 subheading inversion keeps big type calm and small type punchy.
- Never outline the secondary button in a 1px border on white — the secondary action is solid #000000 at identical geometry, so hierarchy reads through hue, not fill.

## Elevation

- **Form controls, rating chips, floating help button:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 1px 0px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.16) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.08) 0px 3px 9px 0px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.08) 0px 2px 5px 0px`
- **Compact controls with a shallower drop (single use):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 1px 0px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.16) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(61, 59, 53, 0.08) 0px 2px 5px 0px`
- **Feature cards and product mockup window:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.09) 0px 3px 12px 0px`
- **Highlight card ring (the outlier):** `rgb(248, 28, 229) 0px 0px 0px 2px, rgba(248, 28, 229, 0.36) 0px 0px 0px 4px`

The rule: small interactive controls get a warm 1px ring with stacked soft drops, large containers get one diffuse 12px blur, and color enters elevation exactly once.

## Imagery

The page has no photography. Imagery is split between product reconstructions and hand-drawn illustration. The hero and feature cards embed live-looking editor UI: a browser frame with #dfdfde dots, a 10px radius, a 2px #37352f17 border and shadow md, plus mockup-internal pastel field tags in yellow, blue, pink and green that are not system tokens. Around them, ballpoint doodles of faces, speech bubbles reading "Yes!" and "NOP.", stars and confetti dashes float in the margins in #37352f, with short #f81ce5 strokes. Feature icons are 16px single-weight line glyphs in #f81ce5. The only gradient is the decorative violet-to-magenta title on the highlight card, which is not a token. Customer logos are monochrome. The narrative is a person sketching in the margins while the software does the work.

## Layout

Content sits in a centered column with a 976px max-width (h1 973px, footer 976px), while text blocks cap at 600px and cards span roughly 650px at desktop. The nav is static, not sticky, 60px tall and filled #ffffff, with the hand-lettered wordmark left and Pricing, Log in, Sign up and the blue Create form pill right. The hero is centered: a 64px headline, a 22px lede, a 36px CTA with 13px microcopy, then the mockup window, with doodles floating in both gutters. Sections then shift to left-aligned headings with 192px gaps. Features run as one full-width highlight card, a two-column card grid, then full-width demo cards. Logos form a single row of seven. The footer is an open, borderless-topped link index with 100px padding. At 375px, set the hero at 36px (heading-lg), collapse the grid to one column and use 64px section gaps. Overall density: spacious.

## Marginalia Discipline

The illustration layer is the brand. Every doodle is single-weight ballpoint linework in #37352f, roughly 2px, with no fills except dotted stipple and no shading. Magenta #f81ce5 appears only as short dashes, crosses and underlines, never as an object color. The discipline breaks the moment someone commissions a polished 3D mascot, adds flat-color spot illustrations, or animates the doodles into bouncing characters, because the sketches must look like they were made with a pen in five seconds. To extend it, draw new doodles in the same line weight. Keep them in the page gutters or inside card lower halves, never behind body text. Limit magenta to 10% or less of the stroke count of any drawing, so the highlighter stays an accent rather than a palette.

## Ink Temperature

Two blacks run the page. Warm #37352f is the reading ink (120 uses), and pure #000000 is reserved for headings. All neutrals, from #45433e and #5f5e5a to #777672 and the #37352f17 hairline, share the same warm, slightly olive cast, and the shadows tint toward the same 61,59,53 brown. This is the same document-editor heritage that makes the product feel familiar to Notion users. The system breaks when a cool slate gray or a blue-gray border enters, because the warm and cool mix reads as two products stitched together. Extend it by deriving any new neutral from #37352f at a stated opacity (for example 9% for lines, as the hairline already does) rather than by picking a fresh gray from a generic palette.

## Two-Hue Budget

Exactly two saturated hues exist, and their jobs never overlap. #0070d7 means "do something" and appears only on clickable fills and links. #f81ce5 means "notice this" and appears only on strokes, icons and one ring. Everything else is warm neutral, which makes the 36px CTA the most findable object on a page full of drawings. The budget breaks if a third hue arrives for success states or badges, or if blue starts decorating headings. Extend it by expressing status through neutrals plus iconography first. If a status color becomes unavoidable, confine it to a 6px dot inside the product UI and keep it off the marketing canvas entirely.

## Similar Brands

- **Notion** — It shares the exact #37352f warm body ink and the "type it like a doc" block metaphor. Notion uses more black-and-white illustration, while Tally adds a magenta highlighter.
- **Typeform** — It is the direct form-builder competitor. Typeform leans on full-bleed color fields and large imagery, whereas Tally deliberately stays on white paper with 36px controls.
- **Excalidraw** — It shares the hand-drawn, single-stroke sketch aesthetic as a deliberate signal of informality. Tally confines the sketches to margins around precise UI.
- **Basecamp** — It shares quirky doodle illustrations on a light canvas paired with plain-spoken copy, though Basecamp uses a warmer multi-hue palette.
- **Fillout** — It is a genuine form-builder rival with a white canvas and blue CTA. Fillout uses polished product renders where Tally uses ballpoint marginalia.
